carousels.name: You slipped - the binge after is the real danger

slides.title: You slipped. Now comes the [[dangerous part.]]
slides.sub: It's not the slip. It's what you do in the next 24 hours.

slides.title: The "[[screw it]]" voice
slides.body:
"Streak's gone anyway, might as well go all night."

Many people say the binge after a slip does more damage than the slip itself.

slides.title: One slip is [[data,]] not a verdict
slides.body: A slip tells you when, where and why your defenses failed. Shame tells you nothing. It just makes the next urge louder.

slides.title: How one slip becomes a [[week]]
slides.body: Break the chain at step 2. Don't feed the shame.

slides.title: Your first [[24 hours]] after
items: Close the tab, then leave the room.
Write down the trigger: time, place, mood.
Eat, drink water, move for 10 minutes.
Tell one person, or note it in your journal.
slides.note: Be honest: have you binged after a slip before? Drop "yes" below 👇

slides.title:
A slip isn't the end.
[[Quitting is.]]
slides.lead: Panic button for the urge, journaling for the trigger and shame-free support. Private by design.

carousels.name: HALT - your urge may not be about p*rn

slides.title: That urge isn't about p*rn. It's about [[one of 4 things.]]
slides.sub: Most people never check. Do this first.

slides.title: [[Hungry]]
slides.body: Low energy makes your brain hunt for a fast reward. Before you fight the urge, eat something real. Seriously.

slides.title: [[Angry]]
slides.body: Stress and frustration look for relief. P*rn becomes the exit. Name the feeling out loud: "I am angry." Many people find that loosens its grip.

slides.title: [[Lonely]] or [[Tired]]
slides.body: Late, alone, drained: the classic danger zone. Many people report their worst urges hit right here. Text someone. Or go to bed. Both beat the tab.

slides.title: Your [[HALT]] reset
items: Pause for 60 seconds. Don't decide yet.
Ask: hungry, angry, lonely or tired?
Fix that one thing first.
Then check if the urge is still there.
slides.note: Which one gets you most? H, A, L or T? Comment your letter 👇

slides.title:
Meet the urge with a plan,
[[not panic.]]
slides.lead: A panic button for urges, daily guided audio and a community that gets it.

slides.title: You quit p*rn. Now you're [[doomscrolling 6 hours.]]
slides.sub: Congrats. You swapped one loop for another.

slides.title: Same loop, [[new door]]
slides.body:
Reels, shorts, games, snacks. If it's endless and on-demand, your brain may treat it like the old hit.

Many people in recovery describe exactly this.

slides.title: The tell: you feel [[worse]] after
slides.body: Real rest leaves you calmer. If you feel numb, foggy or guilty afterward, it's an escape, not a break.

slides.title: Why it keeps happening
slides.body: You removed the habit but not the feeling it was covering.

slides.title: Fill the [[gap]] on purpose
items: Pick 2 replacements before the urge hits.
Set app time limits, ask a friend for the passcode.
Phone charges outside the bedroom.
Ask what you're avoiding in that moment.
slides.note: What's your replacement habit right now? Confess below 👇

slides.title:
Don't just quit.
[[Rebuild your days.]]
slides.lead: A step-by-step recovery program with guided audio and daily actions, so empty time has a plan.

carousels.name: Hiding it hurts more than the p*rn

slides.title: She didn't leave over the p*rn. She left over the [[lying.]]
slides.sub: Why secrecy is often the bigger wound.

slides.title: The [[betrayal]] is the secret
slides.body:
Many partners say the dishonesty hurt more than the p*rn itself.

Every "I'm fine" and deleted history adds up.

slides.title: It's not [[about them]]
slides.body: Partners often blame themselves, wondering if they weren't enough. They didn't cause this. And you can't recover while hiding it.

slides.title: The secrecy [[cycle]]
slides.body: Shame feeds the thing you're ashamed of. Honesty breaks it.

slides.title: Rebuilding [[trust]]
items: Tell the truth before you're caught.
Don't promise "never again". Show a plan.
Let progress be visible, not just claimed.
Get support beyond your partner.
slides.note: Partners and quitters: what helped you rebuild trust? Share below 👇

slides.title:
Recovery works better
[[out in the open.]]
slides.lead: 1-on-1 accountability, public habit tracking so a partner can see progress, and an anonymous community.

slides.title: Day 30 hits. Then [[December]] hits you.
slides.sub: Why the challenge ending is the riskiest moment.

slides.title: The [[reward]] trap
slides.body:
"I made it, I deserve it."

Treating p*rn as a prize for finishing keeps it at the center of your life.

slides.title: A challenge is [[not]] a plan
slides.body: Countdowns end. Habits don't. If the only plan was "white-knuckle till the 30th", nothing is left for Day 31.

slides.title: The post-challenge [[crash]]
slides.body: Plenty of people report this exact pattern. You can plan around it.

slides.title: Plan Day [[31]] now
items: Set a new goal before the 30th: 60 or 90 days.
Keep your blocker on. Don't celebrate by removing it.
Pick a reward that isn't p*rn.
Keep your daily routine exactly the same.
slides.note: What's your Day 31 plan? Tell us below 👇

slides.title:
Don't end at 30.
[[Keep going.]]
slides.lead: A guided daily program that keeps going after the challenge, with streaks and support when urges hit.
